neighbours.label: Daoism: the Dao (Tao) as 'the Way', Laozi, the Tao Te Ching (Daodejing) and Zhuangzi, in English and in Chinese (道, 老子); Confucian and Buddhist teaching and the ordinary English 'way' stay low
fire: The sage taught that the Tao flows like water, yielding yet unstoppable.
Translations of the Tao Te Ching outnumber those of almost any other book.
Laozi is said to have written his book at a mountain pass before vanishing west.
Taoist priests chant verses from the Daodejing at the temple.
Zhuangzi's stories mock rulers who cling to power instead of following the Dao.
In Daoism, acting without forcing, wu wei, is the highest skill.
她每天早上读一章《道德经》。
quiet: The sage taught that the river flows like time, yielding yet unstoppable.
Translations of the Analects outnumber those of almost any other book.
Confucius is said to have edited his books at the court of Lu.
Buddhist monks chant verses from the Heart Sutra at the temple.
Mencius's stories praise rulers who care for the people instead of clinging to power.
In tennis, hitting without forcing is the highest skill.
她每天早上读一章《论语》。
neighbours.short: Daoism (the Dao, Laozi, the Tao Te Ching)
